messages:
maria: heads up — eu-west3 GPU attaches started failing ~10m ago. seeing local nvme iops pinned and a raft of fsync timeouts. provisioning backlog growing. anyone else? :grimacing:

ashwin: yup saw the spike on cluster-metrics. which pool? scratchpool-eu-west3?

maria: scratchpool-eu-west3 and a few preemptible pools. small jobs queuing, larger gpu jobs failing attach. quick excerpt from node `/var/log/kern.log`:
```
[17235.123456] nvme0: io submit failed: -11
[17235.123457] fsync: 500ms stall (ts=17235)
[17236.000001] attach: timeout waiting for block device
```

ben: can you paste `iostat -x 1 3` from a hot node? trying to see util% and await.

maria: paste below (hot node gnode-32):
```
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rsec/s  wsec/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await  svctm  util
nvme0n1        0.00   0.00  10.0 320.0  400.0  25600.0   78.0    12.4   18.2   2.4   22.9   0.12  99.6
```

olga: that avgqu-sz and util looks brutal. scrub/janitor likely overlapped with a batch surge. did we run the nightly deep-scrub earlier than usual?

maria: yes — scrub window was shifted earlier in the rollout (ops change) and coincided with a spiky job ramp.

ben: immediate mitigation: throttle janitor scrubs in eu-west3 and bump scrub nice/IO weight. we can also temporarily widen attach timeout for the attach controller. both low-risk.

ashwin: agree. quick kube patch for janitor configmap:
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch cm janitor-config -p '{"data":{"scrub_io_limit":"50mbps","scrub_concurrency":"1"}}'
```
That should throttle IO usage. I'll run it if someone gives :+1:.

maria: +1 do it. also plan to evict a couple of heavy preemptible batches manually.

janitor-bot: [automated] scrub-run throttling enabled in eu-west3: scrub_io_limit=50mbps, scrub_concurrency=1 by ashwin at 2025-09-19T14:05:24Z :gear:

olga: cc @sre-oncall to monitor attaches. we should also add a short-term workaround to route new attaches to zone-b which still has spare iops headroom. routing rule can be adjusted in the scheduler: set region_affinity to prefer zone-b if io_util>85%.

ben: long-term: we need smarter scrub placement (avoid hot stripe nodes) and better preemption smoothing for janitor windows. also consider increasing scrub incremental chunking so it yields more often to attach-critical flows.

ashwin: noted for postmortem. for now i've increased attach timeout from 30s -> 60s in the controller config (will roll next 5min):
```yaml
controller:
  attach_timeout_sec: "60"
```

maria: attach failures dropped after throttle + timeout bump. attach backlog cleared in ~6m. still need a follow-up to avoid repeating.

olga: can we add a short playbook: detection rule (nvme util>90% && attach_errors>5/min) -> auto-throttle janitor + increase attach_timeout + notify oncall?

ben: yep. i'll draft the playbook and include cost tradeoffs (throttling scrubs delays wear reporting, extends retention of tempfiles causing storage tax).

maria: one more note — found 2 nodes with soft checksum errors during the spike, probably from queued fsyncs racing with scrub deletes. opened a ticket to run `nvme smart-log` and mark for close monitoring.
